overall: Los Angeles is experiencing an unusually cool, marine-layer-dominated morning on June 25, with temperatures locked tightly in the 62-63°F range since midnight and essentially zero warming velocity as of 09:35 ET. Dense patchy fog and persistent SW onshore flow are suppressing heating, and the running max of 63°F has not budged in hours — a textbook 'June Gloom' pattern holding firm well into the morning.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show moderate spread: HRRR is the most aggressive at 70.2°F, ECMWF at 68.4°F, and NBM at 67.0°F — all clustering in the upper 60s to low 70s, well above current observations. The intraday model, anchored by the flat temperature trace and strong marine layer, is pulling probabilities toward the 70-81°F range, while the META fused model concentrates mass in the 70-79°F zone, suggesting models expect a delayed but meaningful afternoon burn-off.
max_temp_prediction: Given the persistent marine layer, near-zero warming velocity through mid-morning, and NWS forecast of a high near 69°F, the most likely outcome is a TMAX in the 68-72°F range. The META model's modal buckets (70-79°F each ~14-16%) and the NWP model consensus around 68-70°F support a best estimate near 70°F, with meaningful uncertainty toward the mid-70s if fog clears decisively by early afternoon. Confidence is moderate — the flat obs-to-now argue for the lower end, but models consistently project more warming than currently observed.
